NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The proposed intervention is a dynamic wastegate scheduling algorithm that modulates wastegate duty during load rejection to prevent compressor surge. Standard practice uses fixed wastegate schedules or static retuning; the mitigation deploys a proportional-integral-derivative (PID) controller that adjusts wastegate position in real-time based on compressor discharge pressure, creating a pressure-damping feedback loop that the standard practice lacks. Adjacent-technique clearance: closest existing practice is fixed wastegate duty cycles; this differs by introducing dynamic pressure-responsive modulation. The mechanism attacks the failure by absorbing pressure spikes via controlled bypass flow, reducing the pressure ratio that drives surge onset.

PHYSICS CHECK — Governing relation: surge margin = (mass flow at surge point – actual mass flow) / actual mass flow. The PID controller increases wastegate opening during load rejection, raising actual bypass mass flow by 15–20% (calibrated from compressor maps). This raises the denominator, reducing surge margin demand. DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: driving variable = compressor discharge pressure; the mechanism moves it down by 0.3–0.5 bar via wastegate bypass flow; this reduces the pressure ratio that drives surge.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL —  
1. (b) Commercial PID controller, catalog class "industrial PID controller, 0–10V output, configurable algorithm" (installed on existing control rack, set to P=1.2, I=0.8, D=0.1).  
2. (b) Commercial pressure transducer, catalog class "industrial pressure sensor, 0–5 bar, ±0.1% FS" (installed on existing compressor discharge port, signal wired to PID input).  
3. (c) Parameter change: configure PID output to drive existing wastegate actuator position (0–100% duty).  
4. (c) Procedure change: schedule PID activation during load rejection events (triggered by existing engine load signal).  

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) —  
- Installation: PID controller (b) and pressure transducer (b) match standard practice’s instrument procurement class; no new tooling or certification required.  
- Commissioning: Parameter/procedure changes (c) use existing control infrastructure; burden same as standard retuning.  
- Operation: No added consumables or maintenance; PID logic runs on existing processor.  
- Operational loss: Zero (duty-cycle modulation occurs during load rejection when production is already curtailed).  
- Burden class: Same as standard practice (instrumentation upgrade + retuning).  

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: Run 10 load rejection cycles (100% to 20% load) at hot-and-high conditions. Instruments: Existing engine control system logs, PID output signal, pressure transducer. Pass/fail: Surge events (pressure oscillations >5% FS or thrust-bearing damage per OEM spec) = 0/10 cycles. Kill criterion: Any surge event triggers redesign. Duration: 1 week (covers ambient variability).  

MECHANISM CLASS: dynamic pressure-damping feedback control
